Definition: to be (causatively, make or act) circumspect and hence, intelligent
BiblicalUsage: Sâkal carries the sense of to be (causatively, make or act) circumspect and hence, intelligent. In 1 Chronicles 28:19, we read, "…LORD made me understand in writing by hand…"; in 1 Kings 2:3, "…keep the charge of the LORD thy God…". You hear it again in 1 Samuel 18:5 — "…out whithersoever Saul sent him, behaved himself wisely…" — and in 2 Chronicles 30:22, "…eat throughout the feast seven days, offering peace…".
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that sâkal is no accident in the text, and it names something real, and God does not use empty words. And I hold that sâkal is as true now as when it was first written, because God does not change.
